t: Shansabani chiefs from the mountains of Ghor rose from Ghaznavid vassals to rulers of an empire from Khurasan to Bengal.
Mu'izz al-Din won the Second Battle of Tarain in 1192, and his slave generals went on to found the Delhi Sultanate.
The Minaret of Jam, about 65 metres high, survives in a remote Afghan valley as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
dyk: In northern India the Ghurid sultan Mu'izz al-Din Muhammad issued gold coins bearing the image of the Hindu goddess Lakshmi, following local coin designs.
ev: Mahmud of Ghazni invades Ghor and captures its chief, Muhammad ibn Suri
Ala al-Din Husayn burns Ghazni for seven days, earning the name 'World Burner'
Mu'izz al-Din takes Ghazni and makes it his base for campaigns in India
The Ghurids take Lahore, ending Ghaznavid rule
Mu'izz al-Din defeats Prithviraj Chauhan at the Second Battle of Tarain
The Khwarazmshah and the Qara Khitai defeat Mu'izz al-Din at Andkhud
Mu'izz al-Din is assassinated; Qutb al-Din Aybak takes power at Lahore
The Khwarazmian Empire takes Ghazni, ending Ghurid rule
